about.title: What is Soleon?
about.subtitle: Transparent launch, verifiable operations and final protocol immutability
about.description: Soleon separates protocol rules from launch operations. Soleon Maintainer publishes the website, reports and temporary wallets, while the on-chain staking rules are designed to become immutable after the ten-wave monitoring window and final audit.
about.feature1Desc: 4,000,000 SEON are transferred directly to 400 independently selected Solana wallets in ten weekly waves. Recipients do not connect, sign, claim or pay.
about.feature2Desc: Source code, selection rules, snapshot, seed, wave reports, addresses, balances and authority status are published for independent verification.
about.feature3Desc: The staking upgrade authority is retained only through the disclosed ten-wave correction window. After the final audit, critical authorities are revoked and the on-chain rules become fixed.

tokenomics.subtitle: Token distribution and emission
tokenomics.emissionDesc: Single 7-day lock. Rewards are distributed proportionally to active staking from a finite reward vault and a verifiable annual budget.

phases.phase2Desc: Staking opens with wave 1. Forty selected wallets receive 10,000 SEON each week while cumulative reports and any verified correction remain public.

phases.phase3Desc: After cumulative verification and the final audit, critical staking authorities are revoked. A later pool is optional and requires observed activity plus permanently locked or burned LP.

ecosystem.title: Soleon Ecosystem
ecosystem.subtitle: Mechanisms designed for long-term sustainability
ecosystem.stakingDesc: Lock for 7 days. Rewards accrue proportionally to active SEON from an annual budget limited by the reward vault.
ecosystem.renewalDesc: An on-time renew compounds principal and rewards and lowers redistribution on future claims by 0.5 percentage points, from the initial 10% toward 0%.
ecosystem.feeDesc: Transfer fee starts at 0%. Once staking is deployed and opened, anyone may permissionlessly activate 0.02%; it then rises by another 0.02 points per year up to 0.4%. 20% is burned and the remainder returns to rewards except for the fixed 1 SEON caller reward.

philosophy.title: The Soleon Philosophy
philosophy.intro: Soleon was not born to promise quick riches. It was born to test whether a token can sustain itself with clear rules, open distribution, public review and without an administrator capable of changing the system after launch.
philosophy.marketDecides: The market will decide if this model deserves adoption. Soleon can only offer transparency, economic design, open code, public review and immutability.
philosophy.card1Desc: No future price or enrichment is promised.
philosophy.card2Desc: Important rules live in the contract and can be reviewed publicly.
philosophy.card3Desc: Adoption depends on users, liquidity, trust and real utility.
philosophy.whatItSolvesDesc: Many tokens depend on promises, opaque teams, closed presales or liquidity controlled by a few. Soleon tries to do the opposite: public rules, reviewable code, no-sale distribution, open testing and a contract that ends without a mutable administrator.
philosophy.sustainableDesc: Sustainable does not mean the price always goes up. It means the system rules try to balance rewards, staking, fees, burns, public review, interface maintenance and possible community liquidity without depending on constant private decisions.

stakingUtility.title: Staking as core utility
stakingUtility.intro: Soleon is designed around staking. It is not an added feature: it is the main utility of the token.
stakingUtility.description: Staking means locking SEON for 7 days. The protocol distributes rewards according to public rules and proportionally to active principal.
stakingUtility.rewardsExplanation: After the initial bootstrap distribution, staking will be the main mechanism to access SEON reserved as rewards. These tokens already exist in a public reserve and are distributed according to contract rules.
stakingUtility.card1Title: The token is used by locking it
stakingUtility.card1Desc: Staking gives direct utility to SEON: users can lock their tokens to participate in the rewards system.
stakingUtility.card2Desc: Staking rewards do not depend on infinite minting: they come from an existing reserve distributed by verifiable rules.
stakingUtility.card3Desc: After lock there is a 3-day grace period. Later, a position can be renewed, unstaked or publicly cleaned.
stakingUtility.warning: SEON rewards do not guarantee economic profit. USD value depends on the market.

guides.liquidityGuideTitle: How to understand, create and provide liquidity
guides.liquidityGuideSubtitle: Participate in community pools while understanding fees, liquidity control and risk
guides.liquidityGuideIntro: Providing liquidity means depositing two assets, for example SEON and USDC, into a pool. Other users swap against that pool and pay trading fees. As an LP you can receive part of those fees from your own position, but you also take price risk, impermanent-loss risk and DEX risk. It is not guaranteed yield.
guides.lpFeesDesc: Each pool has its own trading fee. When someone buys or sells through that pool, they pay a small fee. That fee is distributed to liquidity providers according to their position size and the DEX rules. Higher volume can generate more fees; if there is little volume, there are few relevant fees.
guides.createPoolDesc: Raydium, Orca and Meteora allow pools to be created through their own interfaces. The creator chooses the pair, pool type and parameters under the DEX rules. Soleon will link official documentation and display reviewed pools, but it will not impose a platform or a specific fee.
guides.poolTrustTitle: Avoid relying on a single wallet
guides.poolTrustDesc: A pool can lose depth if one person withdraws their position. Multiple contributing wallets or a verifiable locking mechanism are preferable when supported by the DEX. A listed pool still carries risk: always check who controls liquidity and whether it can be withdrawn.
guides.communityCreationStep1Desc: Agree on the pair and DEX with several people before creating the pool. Splitting contributions reduces reliance on one wallet.
guides.communityCreationStep2Desc: Create the pool through the official DEX interface and provide from each wallet. Review pool type, parameters and fee before signing.
guides.communityCreationStep3Desc: Share the address, mint, liquidity control and links. The website may display it with its classification and direct access after review.
guides.cpmmGuideDesc: Liquidity is available across the full price range. It is less efficient than concentrated liquidity, but simpler, easier to understand and suitable for a new token with an unstable early price.
guides.dammGuideDesc: Meteora's dynamic pool model. It can be useful if it supports permanently locked liquidity and automatic compounding of LP fees inside the pool.
guides.clmmGuideDesc: Liquidity concentrated inside a price range. It can be more efficient while price stays inside the range, but requires choosing and managing that range.
guides.cpmmHowDesc: You usually deposit both assets in the pair, for example SEON and USDC, in proportion to the pool price. Your liquidity remains active across the full price range. It is simpler and requires less maintenance.
guides.dammHowDesc: For users it feels similar to an AMM: you deposit assets into a pool. The difference is that Meteora can allow dynamic configurations, such as automatic fee compounding or more flexible parameters depending on the pool.
guides.clmmHowDesc: Besides providing assets, you choose a price range. Your liquidity only works inside that range. If price moves outside, you may stop earning fees and become mainly exposed to one of the two assets.
guides.whyCpmmDesc: If the community creates an AMM pool, a CPMM may be a simple option because it keeps liquidity across the full price range and reduces active management. Soleon has not selected an official pool.
guides.clmmRiskDesc: If the range is narrow and price moves, the position can become concentrated in one asset, stop earning fees and increase impermanent-loss impact. That is why CLMM fits better as a secondary pool with a wide range.
guides.impermanentLossDesc: Impermanent loss happens when you provide two assets to a pool and their relative price changes. The pool automatically adjusts its balances: if SEON rises significantly, your position may end with less SEON and more USDC than if you had simply held both assets outside the pool. Fees can offset part or all of that effect, but it is not guaranteed. In CLMM with narrow ranges this effect can feel stronger because the position is concentrated in a specific price zone.
guides.dexDocsWarning: These links lead to external documentation. Soleon does not control Raydium, Meteora or Orca. Always verify the official URL before connecting a wallet or adding liquidity.

markets.subtitle: SEON starts DEX-first. A separately published temporary reserve may place genuine SEON/USDC orders under fixed rules; it never self-trades, fabricates volume or promises liquidity.
markets.mintAddressDesc: Always verify the mint address before swapping. Copy and check on Solscan.
markets.mintPending: Pending - available when the SEON mint is published
markets.verifyWarningDesc: Anyone can create pools with fake tokens or very low liquidity. Always check that the pool mint matches the official SEON mint shown above.
markets.dexFirstDesc: Soleon does not depend on a CEX listing, private sale or official starting price. The initial target is a verifiable SEON/USDC Manifest order book with public reserve activity clearly separated from third-party activity.
markets.organicMarketDesc: The reserve may quote real bids and asks, but trades occur only against independent counterparties. If nobody trades, reported volume is zero.
markets.verifiedMarketsDesc: The website will only link markets and pools after publishing their on-chain addresses and reviewing that they use the correct SEON mint.
markets.noCustodyDesc: The website does not receive funds or execute trades. Each user signs from their own wallet using external DEX interfaces.
markets.noOfficialLiquidityNote: There is no promised price or guaranteed depth. Reserve orders are disclosed as Soleon-controlled liquidity and never presented as organic demand.
markets.liquidityGuideCtaTitle: Want to understand, create or provide liquidity?

markets.noSwapIntegration: Buying SEON, selling SEON, providing liquidity, managing LP positions and claiming LP fees will happen through Jupiter, Raydium, Meteora, Orca or another verified external interface. Soleon does not operate a centralized exchange.
markets.lpBenefit1: Lets buyers and sellers trade without relying on a CEX
markets.lpBenefit2: Deeper pools reduce slippage and price manipulation
markets.lpBenefit3: LPs can earn trading fees from their own positions
markets.lpBenefit4: On-chain visible liquidity helps keep the market verifiable

markets.lpRisk5: Concentrated liquidity can move out of range and stop earning fees

markets.poolPendingDesc: No verified pool exists for this DEX yet.

markets.verificationRule1: The pool uses the official SEON mint published on this page.
markets.verificationRule2: The pair and DEX are clear, preferably SEON/SOL or SEON/USDC on known infrastructure.
markets.verificationRule3: Liquidity and volume can be checked on Solscan or in the DEX interface.
markets.verificationRule4: It shows whether liquidity is locked, burned, multisig-controlled or freely removable.
markets.verificationRule5: There are no signs of immediate extraction, wrong mint or suspicious routing.
markets.verificationRule6: External links point to the real pool, not generic pages or clones.
markets.labelVerifiedDesc: Correct mint, known DEX and consistent on-chain data.
markets.labelCommunityDesc: User-created pool with correct mint, but without strong guarantees.
markets.labelHighRiskDesc: Low liquidity, unlocked liquidity, new pool or weak conditions.
markets.labelFakeDesc: Wrong mint or clear attempt to confuse users.
markets.liquidityInterestDesc: Planned feature for the community to coordinate interest without sending funds to Soleon. It will be a public signal, not a deposit or obligation.
markets.interestStep1Desc: The wallet signs a message with desired pair, preferred DEX and approximate amount.
markets.interestStep2Desc: Nobody sends SOL, USDC or SEON to Soleon. Liquidity is provided from each wallet on the chosen DEX.
markets.interestStep3Desc: Once there is enough interest, the community may decide to create a pool and request public review.
markets.liquidityInterestWarning: The interest list does not guarantee price, liquidity or rewards. It only helps show whether enough potential LPs exist to create a healthy pool.
markets.fakePoolDesc: A pool named SEON is not enough. If the mint does not match, liquidity is tiny or LP can be removed without notice, the website will mark it as high risk or fake and will not use it as a primary link.
markets.manifestDesc: Initial DEX target: a verifiable on-chain order book where the public reserve and independent users may place genuine limit orders.
markets.manifestWhatDesc: Manifest is a Solana order-book DEX. As on a CEX, buyers and sellers place orders with an amount and price; a trade occurs when compatible orders match.
markets.manifestHowDesc: Market logic executes on-chain and each user trades from their own wallet. Soleon does not receive deposits, hold funds or decide which order should execute.
markets.manifestWhyDesc: It supports transparent price discovery without a presale or a large creator-funded AMM pool. Reserve balances and orders remain publicly attributable.
markets.manifestOrderBookNote: Orders do not guarantee a counterparty or liquidity. Price forms when buyers and sellers agree to trade.
markets.transferFeeWarning: SEON uses Token-2022. The applicable transfer fee follows the protocol's public schedule and may affect the net amount received.
markets.communityPoolsDesc: An AMM pool is optional and considered only after real activity has established observable trading conditions. No pool or initial valuation is promised.
markets.communityPoolsWhatDesc: A pool holds two assets, for example SEON and USDC. Swaps execute against that reserve and pay a pool-defined fee; under the DEX rules, part of those fees belongs to liquidity providers.
markets.communityPoolsWhyDesc: An AMM pool is considered only after two to three months of real activity. If created with remaining reserve assets, its price must follow observed trading and its LP must be permanently burned or locked.
markets.communityPoolsHowDesc: Multiple contributing wallets or verifiable locking mechanisms are preferable when available. This reduces reliance on one person who could withdraw their entire position.
markets.communityPoolsGuideTitle: Create or provide liquidity through a DEX
markets.communityPoolsGuideDesc: The website helps explain the process and links official documentation. It does not choose the DEX, pool type or fee for the community.
markets.communityPoolsPending: No reviewed AMM pool has been published. A pool will not be forced without sufficient real activity.

maintenance.title: Protocol Maintenance
maintenance.subtitle: Permissionless maintenance actions that help keep the Soleon protocol running. Anyone can execute these actions - the connected wallet signs transactions but does not receive admin power.
maintenance.whatIsThisDesc: These are public protocol actions that anyone can execute. Your wallet signs the transaction, but you do not gain any special privileges. The same permissionless instructions can be called outside this website using the published Program ID and IDL.
maintenance.permissionlessNote: All actions on this page are permissionless. Anyone can call the same instructions directly on-chain without using this website.
maintenance.feeUpdatePendingNotice: The update is already sent. Solana can take a little while to reflect it on-chain.
maintenance.connectRequiredDesc: Connect your wallet to execute maintenance actions. You will sign transactions but not gain any admin privileges.
maintenance.updateFeeDesc: Permissionless function: activates 0.02% when staking opens and then allows a yearly increase under the published schedule.
maintenance.dynamicFeeExplanation: Mint starts with a 0% fee. When staking opens, anyone may permissionlessly update it to 0.02%. It then increases by another 0.02 points every 365 days up to 0.4%.
maintenance.maxFeeCapInfo: Absolute cap: {maxFee} SEON per transfer (protects very large transfers).
maintenance.actionsNotActiveYet: These actions will be available when the final token and staking are active.
maintenance.feeUpdateNotAvailable: Fee update is only available after the staking program is deployed and staking opens. The first update activates 0.02%; later updates are yearly.
maintenance.maxFeeReached: Fee has reached the maximum of 0.4%. No more updates are allowed.
maintenance.feeDistributionDesc: Collects Token-2022 withheld fees and distributes them by fixed protocol rules: 20% burned, 1 SEON caller reward, rest goes to staking rewards.
maintenance.feeCollectionExplanation: First, the fees withheld in the SEON mint's Token-2022 accounts are harvested. Then they are distributed: at exactly the 200 SEON minimum, the split equals 79.5% rewards, 20% burn, 0.5% caller. Above that minimum, the caller still receives 1 SEON fixed and the excess goes to staking rewards.
maintenance.connectToSeeCooldown: Connect wallet to see your cooldown
maintenance.feeScanUnavailableDesc: To collect fees, the interface needs to detect which Token-2022 accounts have withheld fees. Some public RPCs don't index Token-2022 accounts for this type of search. If the index is unavailable, the protocol still works, but this action can't be prepared from the web until using a compatible RPC/indexer.
maintenance.feeScanPendingDesc: The mint/RPC may be configured, but the interface is not reading a scan of Token-2022 accounts with withheld fees yet. Amounts will not be shown until that index is connected.
maintenance.infrastructureNote: This is a website infrastructure requirement, not a contract error.
maintenance.pendingSetupDesc: Fee collection will be available when the staking contract is deployed, staking is open, and the fee index is configured.
maintenance.publicActionNote: This is a public action. The fixed 1 SEON reward compensates whoever pays the transaction and helps maintain the protocol. It's not a guaranteed source of income.
maintenance.cooldownInfo: Global cooldown: 1 hour. Per-wallet cooldown: 24 hours.
maintenance.cleanupDesc: Public batch closure for positions beyond the 7-day lock and 3-day grace period.
maintenance.cleanupDetected: Positions found by the global scan every 8 hours
maintenance.cleanupExplanation: The website reuses one global scan every 8 hours. Each transaction validates on-chain and closes up to 4 positions; more positions require signing another batch. The 1 SEON incentive can only be paid once every 20 minutes globally. Principal and net rewards always return to the owner. There is no maintenance fee; the caller pays normal Solana gas.
maintenance.interfaceMaintainerDesc: How the official website is maintained
maintenance.interfaceMaintainerExplanation: The Soleon protocol is designed to become immutable and permissionless. The official website is different: it needs technical maintenance so the domain, documentation, RPC endpoints, wallet integrations, DEX links, lock proofs, and frontend code remain usable.
maintenance.maintainerDoes2: Frontend hosting, IPFS, or Arweave releases
maintenance.maintainerDoes4: Wallet adapter and frontend dependency updates
maintenance.maintainerDoes5: Links to official DEX pools, proofs, and explorers
maintenance.maintainerCannotDo1: Change staking rules, annual budget, or lock
maintenance.maintainerCannotDo2: Move protocol reserves or tokens locked in staking
maintenance.maintainerCannotDo3: Mint SEON or withdraw liquidity provided by users
maintenance.maintainerCannotDo5: Give special on-chain privileges to selected users
maintenance.maintenanceWalletDesc: This public wallet receives only the published maintenance fees defined by staking actions. Genesis Airdrop recipients pay no fee. Its balance and movements can be checked on Solscan, and it has no authority over immutable protocol rules.
maintenance.websiteConvenienceNote: The official website is a convenience layer, not a source of protocol authority. After immutability, the same on-chain actions remain callable through the published Program ID, IDL, mint address, and account addresses even if the official website is unavailable.
